newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says deficit may be under C$16 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says deficit may be under C$16 bln.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin, on the election campaign trail, said on Monday that the federal deficit will likely be less than C$16 billion for the 1996-97 fiscal year.
"It would not be unreasonable to assume a deficit of below C$16 billion," Martin told Reuters in a phone interview from Halifax.
He said he was basing his assumption on preliminary deficit numbers for the last quarter of the fiscal year, which ended March 31.

He said he was also basing the number on year-end adjustments made in previous years, which have historically added between C$4 billion and C$6 billion on to the preliminary deficit numbers to come up with the final tally.
He said the official final tally would likely not be available until this fall.
The deficit from April 1996 until February 1997 totalled C$7.83 billion, compared to C$23.28 billion for the same period a year earlier.
The Finance Department had been predicting a 1996-97 deficit of less than C$19 billion.
The government's original goal for the year's deficit was C$24.3 billion.
The governing Liberals called an election on Sunday for June 2. They plan to campaign largely on their economic record.
But earlier on Monday, Prime Minister Jean Chretien said he would reverse planned spending cuts on health care because of the government's success in cutting the deficit.
